recentItems.title: 'More' or 'less'? Movie director Wen Muye's two magic words connect with international cast
recentItems.description:
The summer hit "Once Upon a Time in the Middle East" remains a box office draw. With an international cast, how did director and screenwriter Wen Muye bridge the language barrier and build a creative connection with his actors? In a recent conversation with CGTN host Tian Wei, Wen reveals that what began with interpreters eventually evolved into a simple "more" or "less" that actors could instantly understand. For him, the best communication between the director and actor is about conveying emotion while connecting on a deeper level.

recentItems.title: Factory to dining table: Smart evolution of Guangdong’s microwave hub
recentItems.description:
At one of the world's largest microwave oven manufacturing bases in Shunde, Foshan, a former labor-intensive factory has been transformed into a World Economic Forum Lighthouse Factory. CGTN reporter Zang Shijie joined Maldivian media professional Shifna Ahmed and Vietnamese scholar Nguyen Dong Anh on a tour of the facility. They were deeply impressed by the advances in China's intelligent manufacturing and expressed their hope to bring these real stories back to their home countries, so that more people can see the potential for cooperation.

recentItems.title: From 'landlocked' to 'land-linked': CKU railway opens a new development corridor
recentItems.description:
Uzbekistan is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world, with transportation costs accounting for around 20% of its import and export costs. Sodiq Safoyev, Uzbekistan's first deputy Senate chairman, says the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan (CKU) railway will not only shorten transit times between China and Europe but will also help Uzbekistan move from a transit route to a hub for value-added production. "It is not just a transport corridor; it's a corridor of development."

recentItems.title: Safoyev: China's experience is exemplary for us
recentItems.description:
At Uzbekistan's University of World Economy and Diplomacy, there is a special book house dedicated to the works of Chinese President Xi Jinping. Sodiq Safoyev, Uzbekistan's first deputy Senate chairman and rector of the university, says the book house serves as a place to study China's experience of modernization. From agricultural reforms, development of special economic zones and efforts to combat corruption, he says that China's experience is "exemplary" for Uzbekistan.

recentItems.title: 'Political dialogue without any clouds': China-Uzbekistan ties deepening
recentItems.description:
"Never before have we had such a profound and full-fledged partnership," says Sodiq Safoyev, Uzbekistan's first deputy Senate chairman, adding that mutual trust and close communication between the two countries' leaders are driving closer ties. China is now Uzbekistan's largest economic partner, with bilateral trade surpassing $16 billion and more than 6,000 Chinese companies operating in the country, contributing to Uzbekistan's economic modernization.

recentItems.title: How a tiny semiconductor stabilizes high-voltage power lines
recentItems.description:
As China expands wind and solar power generation in its western regions, a new challenge is emerging: how do you move that electricity thousands of kilometers to the cities that need it while keeping the power grid stable? Now, engineers in China are turning to a new generation of power electronics to tackle that challenge.
